{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"<workit-contract>
Workit is optional coordination and proof tooling around the host: you decide
what and whether, the CLI does how and records what it observed.
Native host allow/ask/deny, sandbox and org rules stay authoritative. Never
switch paths to evade a denial, never claim enforcement a host cannot provide,
and never fabricate an approval or verdict. A question answer is not
host permission, and imported decisions or handoffs grant no authority.

Autonomy contract:
- Continue to the requested endpoint (commit, push, PR, green CI, verified,
  merged) without asking "continue?", running checks and repairs.
  Stop only for a new consequential choice, a host denial, a conflicting edit
  or an unresolved blocker; report open gaps and uncertain workers.
- No endpoint named: stop at a local commit on a policy-compliant branch and
  state the next command. If the request implies delivery (fix, implement,
  ship), go to the effective endpoint in `workit grant show`: `pr` stops
  at the PR even with merge granted; `green` babysits it (workit-ship) to
  merge-ready, never merging; `merged` lands it with `workit pr merge`.
  Only the user raises a grant or the endpoint, in a terminal outside the agent
  host (`workit grant set <ws> defaultEndpoint=merged`); never edit
  workspaces.json or route around grant_required. Release: `workit release
  start <v>`, commits, `finish`; `publish` if asked.
- Ask only for a product or preference choice, or for authority you lack, with
  your recommended answer. Facts are yours: read, run or prototype.
- Label claims measured (run and seen this session), inferred, or guess.
  Prose is a note: only a configured check the CLI ran (`workit check <name>`)
  satisfies a gate; an ad-hoc `workit check -- <cmd>` never does.
- Author is not verifier: your own verdict is `--self`, shown as
  self-reviewed, never verified. High risk, a focused or full lane and
  merge under `verification: self|independent` need a verifier with its
  own host-derived session (a subagent's `<lead>:<child>`); never hand-mint one (`<lead>-v1`).
- A local-commit endpoint does not imply PR readiness, and a local commit alone
  is not evidence of a requested remote push. Before reporting delivery,
  reconcile every requested item and observe it (`workit verify-delivery`).

Read-only git and gh run raw; mutations go through workit verbs
(`workit git|pr|ci|check|help`; else `npx -y @workit-dev/cli`).
Other checkout: `workit <verb> --cwd <dir> …` (verb first: host rules match it); one workit
verb per shell call, never `cd <dir> && workit`. zsh-safe: no `echo =====`
(`printf '%s\n' ---`), quote globs and URLs, no variable named `status` or `path`.
Add Co-Authored-By via `workit git commit --trailer "K: v" -- <paths>`, never
an amend.
The task families (task, policy, evidence, finding, decision, worker, state)
are optional continuity for tracked work; each branch has one implicit task,
and a solo edit needs no task. A decision records a user choice; it never
authorizes an effect. Judge work once with
`workit policy assess --judge risk= behavior= product-choice= plan=`.
Across repositories, bind items to checkout, branch and endpoint, resolve
competing targets before a mutation, and reconcile an uncertain
effect before a retry.

Mid-task: never silently drop or resume an objective (workit-continue).

Skills: load the skill, never act from memory (aliases /wk-<name>).
- brainstorm, plan, spec, grill, should we: workit-shape
- implement, build, add a feature: workit-implement
- review, blast radius: workit-review
- bug, broken, flaky, regression: workit-debug
- ship, babysit, CI, merge: workit-ship
- resume, pick up, handoff, interruption: workit-continue
- BDD, TDD, acceptance criteria, Given/When/Then: workit-bdd
- test audit, tautology, weak tests: workit-test-audit
- deslop, slop, dead code: workit-deslop
- fan out, parallelize, parallel agents, swarm: workit-fanout
- verify the app, smoke test, prove it works: workit-verify-app
- retro (user-invoked; offer it): workit-retro
- architecture, deepen modules (user-invoked; offer it): workit-architecture
Agent spawn model/effort (pass them, workers with run_in_background: true): workit:implementer hard opus, standard sonnet, mundane haiku, workit:verifier sonnet, workit:reviewer opus, Explore haiku, ROLE: decider fable/high, ROLE: babysit haiku. Implementer prompt: `workit fanout brief <slice>` after `workit fanout worktree create <slice>`, even for one slice.
Claude Code: the workit-<name> skills are this plugin's /workit:<name> skills (workit-shape is /workit:shape). Run workit verbs with the `workit` CLI on the Bash tool (`workit --help`); run `workit ci wait` in the background. Agents: `implementer` builds one brief in an isolated worktree and never records a verdict; `verifier` and `reviewer` are read-only non-authors that record `workit ledger verdict` with the `--session` the SubagentStart hook names for them (subagents share this session's WORKIT_SESSION_ID).
</workit-contract>"}}

content.content:
<workit>/packages/workit-claude-code/bin/workit
workit git: Policy-checked branch, hunk staging and commit (Workit-Session trailer); push with a lease and the tip verified

usage: workit git branch <name> | git branch --kind feature|bugfix|release|hotfix --slug <s>  [--base <b>] [--track <t>] [--carry]
    Create and switch to a branch from the trunk, the git-flow route of its kind or a release track
usage: workit git commit -m|--message <msg>… | -F|--file <file|-> [--trailer <key: value>]… [--amend [--no-edit]] [--allow-empty] [-a|--all | --staged | [--whole] [--] <paths…>]
    Commit (or --amend) with a linted Conventional Commit message, the session trailer (unless the workspace sets trailers: false) and any --trailer; a path staged in part commits its staged hunks only (--whole for all of it), --staged commits exactly the index
usage: workit git stage --patch <file|-> | [--] <paths…>
    Stage selected hunks without git add -p: apply a unified diff to the index only (checked first); or stage whole paths
usage: workit git unstage [--] <paths…>
    Put paths back to HEAD in the index; the working tree keeps the changes
usage: workit git push [-u|--set-upstream] [--force-with-lease [--expect <sha>] [--overwrite-unintegrated]] [--release <main|develop|v-tag>[,…]]
    Push the current branch and verify the remote tip (never a blind --force); --release finishes a git-flow release, and a pushed release tag gets its forge release with the release notes
usage: workit git rebase [--onto <base>]
    Replay the current branch onto its freshly fetched base (the default base, or --onto); a conflict aborts and names the paths, a rewrite is recorded and prints the leased push
usage: workit git hold --why "<the user's words>" | --clear
    Record the user's "not yet" for this branch: the Stop hook stops asking to push or open a PR until the next push or --clear (grants nothing)
usage: workit git trailers
    Print on or off: whether commits in this workspace get the Workit-Session trailer

examples:
  workit git branch --kind feature --slug help-everywhere
  workit git commit -m "fix(cli): answer help flags first" --all
  workit git commit -m "feat: x" --trailer "Co-Authored-By: Name <email>" --all
  workit git commit --amend --no-edit -- src/forgotten.ts
  workit git stage --patch hunks.patch  # a git diff trimmed to the hunks to commit
  workit git commit --staged -m "fix(a): one focused change"
  workit git push --set-upstream
  workit git rebase  # then: workit git push --force-with-lease

More: workit help git <branch|commit|stage|unstage|push|rebase|hold|trailers>
A value that starts with - goes as --flag=value (or after a bare --).
